Arm B ran on claude-opus-5; arm A ran on claude-fable-5, because a /model command in an earlier session in that VM had saved Fable 5 as the default for new sessions. The pre-registered consequence is VOID, and it was declared from the config check alone, before the comparison was computed.

The metric is a proxy for steering and this is the gap. NOT amended here: the defect was found AFTER the data existed, unlike amendments A1-A8, and PROTOCOL.md 10.4 is about exactly that. arm_a2.provenance: live run 2026-08-12, same VM reset to the arm-B start state, model pinned via settings.json and --model
arm_a2.VOID: §7.4 froze effort at high, equal across arms. The model was fixed and matched; effort drifted to xhigh because a /effort command in the session saved xhigh as the new default. This is the SECOND harness drift in two runs, both from an in-session settings command whose effect persists. Effort sets the thinking budget, which is a large share of the measured quantity: arm A2's per-phase thinking is 2,240/1,380/1,793 against arm B's 1,513/89/270. The drift plausibly inflates the arm that was predicted to be more expensive, so it biases TOWARD the pre-registered expectation — which is the worst possible direction for a confound to point, and the reason accepting this pair would be indefensible.
arm_a2.verdict: VOID on §7.4. The analyzer additionally returned INDETERMINATE because veto 6 fired on the known-defective human-turns proxy (3 of the 4 plain-string user rows are /effort local-command wrappers; see arm_a.human_turns_note).

observation_not_a_result.why_recorded: The design's own stability checks all passed on this pair, which is information about the INSTRUMENT and not about the controller. It is recorded so that the next run is not the first time anyone sees whether S1 and S2 can agree — and it is labelled here, under a VOID, so that no later reader can quote it as the answer. PROTOCOL.md §10.13 stands: a void pair may not re-price anything.

predictions.why_recorded: PROTOCOL.md §10 names the ways this result could be spun afterwards. A prediction written before the data exists is the cheapest defence against the one it cannot name: quietly discovering that whatever happened is what was expected.
by_claude_before_arm_a: Arm A uses MORE round trips per phase than arm B's 3.00 — the prose orchestrator evaluates gates, writes evidence and tracks budgets in turns the controller replaces with a Node call.
Arm A's per-phase growth exceeds arm B's 5,589, most likely by 1.3x-2.5x.
Arm A's intake mass is 1.5x-6x arm B's 7,294 tokens, depending entirely on how many of the four references it opens.

The sign is NOT uniform across phases: finding 25's mechanism predicts arm B loses at the consensus gate, where its briefing had to be re-derived rather than read (finding 38). Consensus is outside the common scope, so the primary will not see it, and that is a limit of this design and not a result.
predictions.what_would_falsify_the_controller: arm A at or below arm B on either instrument. §5's KILL band is a reachable answer, and the setup was built to let it happen.
